categories.summary: Civil unrest has escalated since late September. Canada's travel advisory reports large demonstrations since late September with looting, vandalism and violent clashes, and localized curfews; 5 November was France's biggest day of protests in years, and clashes continued for a fourth straight weekend. Unions have called further protests for 20–22 November. France has no Country Outlook civil-unrest level yet; its World Map flag is due for re-review by 5 December.
categories.comparison: Civil unrest from late September to mid-November 2026 compared with the preceding months: nationwide demonstrations since late September with looting, violent clashes and local curfews; the biggest single day of protests in years on 5 November (575,000 by the Interior Ministry's count); clashes for a fourth straight weekend on 7–8 November.
categories.levelSummary: Widespread unrest within the last 90 days: about 575,000 marched on 5 November, France's biggest day of protests in years, and clashes recurred for a fourth straight weekend in Paris and Marseille (8 November).
GTI 2026 score 3.224 (rank 35; Institute for Economics & Peace, 2025 data). Terrorism impact is present but not high, and no fatal attack in the last 90 days was documented in this review.

Overall.note: Watchfront raised France to Ongoing Conflict from 23 to 30 October under a temporary civil-unrest review, after protests escalated into riots, looting and confrontations in several major cities. The review expired on 30 October.

Flagged Ongoing Conflict in the 5 November edition under the earlier advisory-based standard, because of severe civil unrest. Under the current standard civil unrest alone does not qualify, and the flag is due for re-review by 5 December.

Methodology correction approved by the owner on 14 November 2026: the Ongoing Conflict flag (set under the earlier advisory-based standard) was removed because civil unrest does not meet Watchfront's conflict standard. France returns to its advisory baseline, Moderate. This corrects the classification method; it is not a security improvement. Civil unrest remains High and deteriorating in Risk Trends.
